scenarios.when_this_applies: Customers outside your company connect their own SurveyMonkey accounts, and you avoid the two approval-gated scopes.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

prerequisites.title: SurveyMonkey account
prerequisites.detail: Anyone with a SurveyMonkey account can register an app.

prerequisites.title: Paid plan with API access
prerequisites.detail: All users of a private app must be on the same team with a paid plan that offers direct API access.

prerequisites.title: Support and account policy
prerequisites.detail: State whether users need a free or paid account with your service, and provide easy-to-find support.

steps.title: Register a SurveyMonkey app
steps.detail: Log in and register a draft app in the developer console. Note the client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: The draft app exists and you have its client ID and secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config for survey_monkey with your client ID and secret. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists in Composio.

steps.title: Register the redirect URI
steps.detail: Paste the Composio redirect URI into the app settings. The redirect_uri in OAuth requests must match the registered one.
steps.done_when: A test OAuth flow returns without a redirect error.

steps.title: Set scopes in app settings
steps.detail: Choose only the scopes you need. Avoid the two approval-gated scopes unless required.
steps.done_when: Scopes are saved in the app settings.

steps.title: Deploy as a private app
steps.detail: Deploy privately. For your own account only, the registration access token can replace the OAuth flow.
steps.done_when: The app works for your team.

steps.title: Draft listing and scope justification
steps.detail: Write an honest English listing with scopes and a use-case summary. Check that the name follows the naming rules.
steps.done_when: The listing text is ready for review.

steps.title: Submit listing for approval
steps.detail: Use the listings tab in My Apps. For the write scopes, contact the help center with your use case.

steps.title: Wait for SurveyMonkey approval
steps.detail: Review time is not documented. Deploy or publish before the 90-day draft period ends.
steps.done_when: The app is approved and published.

traps.title: Draft apps expire after 90 days
traps.detail: Draft apps are disabled if not deployed within 90 days, and other accounts cannot authenticate a draft app.

traps.title: Private apps cannot serve outside customers
traps.detail: A private app serves one account or one Team, and is not eligible for the App Directory.

traps.title: Approval can still be refused
traps.detail: SurveyMonkey may reject an app on criteria not in its checklist. The app must not replicate its survey tools.

traps.title: Users may hit paywalls
traps.detail: Paid-plan scopes make accounts without the plan upgrade to proceed.

traps.title: Call limits are low until published
traps.detail: Draft and private apps start at 120 calls/minute and 500 calls/day, and higher limits may cost extra. Published public apps get up to 500,000 per day.

traps.title: Tokens may expire in future
traps.detail: Access tokens do not currently expire but may in the future.

blockers.what_it_means: SurveyMonkey rejected the app or needs more information.
blockers.what_to_do: Check the listing criteria, fix the issues, and resubmit.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare the listing against the checklist and redraft.

blockers.what_it_means: The user must approve all required scopes and may need a paid plan.
blockers.what_to_do: Mark non-essential scopes optional in app settings.
blockers.agent_can_help: Review the scope settings and suggest which to make optional.

open_questions: How long does public app review take? Not documented; ask SurveyMonkey developer support or watch your first submission.
Which plan do private-app users need? The docs show only 'Sign In to View Plan'; check while logged in or ask sales.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Anyone with a SurveyMonkey account can register an app.
evidence.answer: Anyone with a SurveyMonkey account can register an app.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Registering creates a draft app with an access token you can use to query against your account for 90 days.
evidence.answer: Registering creates a draft app that can be used to query the registering account for 90 days.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Depending on the originating datacenter of the SurveyMonkey account, the API access URL may be different than https://api.surveymonkey.com .
evidence.answer: The API access URL can differ by the SurveyMonkey account's datacenter (EU and Canadian datacenters use different URLs).

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: All apps must be reviewed and approved by SurveyMonkey and adhere to our terms of use before they can be published in our App Directory .
evidence.answer: Public apps must be reviewed and approved by SurveyMonkey, and adhere to its terms of use, before they can be published in the App Directory.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Private apps don’t need to be reviewed by SurveyMonkey.
evidence.answer: Private apps do not need to be reviewed by SurveyMonkey.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: All users of a Private app must belong to the same SurveyMonkey team and have a paid SurveyMonkey plan that offers direct API access .
evidence.answer: Private apps can only be used by users who belong to the same SurveyMonkey team and have a paid plan offering direct API access.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Two scopes, Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys , require SurveyMonkey’s approval to use in a Public app.
evidence.answer: Two scopes (Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys) require SurveyMonkey's approval before a Public app can use them.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: No other SurveyMonkey accounts can authenticate a draft app.
evidence.answer: Other SurveyMonkey accounts cannot authenticate a draft app, so draft apps cannot be used by other organizations without deploying.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Public apps are available to anyone with a SurveyMonkey account and published in our App Directory .
evidence.answer: Public apps are available to anyone with a SurveyMonkey account once published in the App Directory.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: You have a 90-day window to develop in a draft app, after which you’ll need to deploy publicly or privately.
evidence.answer: A draft app has a 90-day development window, after which it must be deployed as Public or Private.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: All apps must be reviewed and approved by SurveyMonkey and adhere to our terms of use before they can be published in our App Directory .
evidence.answer: Public apps must adhere to SurveyMonkey's terms of use in order to be approved and published.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: If you’ve deployed a Public app and want to change your scope requirements to include these, you’ll need to contact us at our help center to tell us more about your app and use case.
evidence.answer: To get approval for the two approval-gated scopes on a deployed Public app, the developer must contact SurveyMonkey's help center and tell them about the app and use case.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Scopes allow apps to access particular resources on behalf of a user.
evidence.answer: Scopes let apps access particular resources on behalf of a user, and users are asked to grant them during OAuth.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Two scopes, Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys , require SurveyMonkey’s approval to use in a Public app.
evidence.answer: Create/Modify Responses and Create/Modify Surveys are the scopes that require SurveyMonkey approval in a Public app.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Some scopes require your app’s users to have a paid SurveyMonkey plan.
evidence.answer: Some scopes require the app's users to have a paid SurveyMonkey plan.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Create/Modify Collectors requires a paid SurveyMonkey plan to create any collector that is not a weblink collector.
evidence.answer: Create/Modify Collectors requires a paid plan to create any collector that is not a weblink collector.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: *Basic plan accounts can access response details for up to 25 responses per survey. Paid plans have unlimited access.
evidence.answer: The responses_read_detail scope (View Response Details) is limited to 25 responses per survey on Basic plan accounts; paid plans have unlimited access.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: All Draft and Private apps will initially be subject to request limits of 120 calls/minute and starting at 500 calls/day ( contact sales ).
evidence.answer: Draft and Private apps initially get request limits of 120 calls per minute and starting at 500 calls per day.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: When a Public app is in draft (during development), it’s subject to draft request limits .
evidence.answer: A Public app in draft (during development) is subject to draft request limits.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Public apps published in our App Directory can make up to 500,000 requests per day to our API.
evidence.answer: Public apps published in the App Directory can make up to 500,000 requests per day.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: We permit three violations of up to 150% within a 30-day window.
evidence.answer: Limits are enforced at 100% only after an app exceeds its limits three times within 30 days; up to three violations of up to 150% are permitted in a 30-day window.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: We begin to enforce limits at 100% once your app exceeds its limits three times within 30 days.
evidence.answer: Enforcement at 100% begins once an app exceeds its limits three times within 30 days.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Before the 90-day draft period ends, you must deploy your app or it’ll be disabled.
evidence.answer: A draft app that is not deployed before the 90-day draft period ends will be disabled.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Our access tokens don’t currently expire but may in the future.
evidence.answer: Access tokens do not currently expire but may in the future, with developers warned before changes.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: SurveyMonkey will review all requests within 5 business days.
evidence.answer: SurveyMonkey says it will review rate-limit increase requests within 5 business days.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Private apps have API request limits and higher limits are available for purchase .
evidence.answer: Private apps have API request limits, and higher limits are available for purchase.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Additional fees may apply for increased rate limits.
evidence.answer: Additional fees may apply for increased rate limits.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Some scopes require your app’s users to have a paid SurveyMonkey plan.
evidence.answer: Some scopes require the app's users to have a paid SurveyMonkey plan, and users may need a paid plan to complete OAuth.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: During the OAuth process, a user is asked to grant permission to scopes your app is requesting access to.
evidence.answer: During OAuth, the user is asked to grant permission to the scopes the app requests.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: If your Public app uses scopes tied to paid plans, any accounts attempting to authenticate without the necessary plan will be asked to upgrade to proceed.
evidence.answer: If a Public app uses paid-plan scopes, accounts without the required plan are asked to upgrade before they can proceed.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: All required scopes must be approved by and available to the user for the OAuth process to succeed.
evidence.answer: All required scopes must be approved by the user and available to them for OAuth to succeed.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: If your app has required scopes , users will need to approve all of them and may need a paid SurveyMonkey plan to successfully OAuth into your app.
evidence.answer: Users must approve all required scopes and may need a paid plan to OAuth into an app with required scopes.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Access tokens can be revoked by the user.
evidence.answer: Users can revoke access tokens, after which the app must complete OAuth again.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: redirect_uri URL encoded OAuth redirect URI you registered for your app (can be found and edited here )
evidence.answer: The redirect_uri must be the URL-encoded OAuth redirect URI registered for the app, which can be found and edited in the app's settings.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: To use our API, you’ll need to register a draft app to your SurveyMonkey account.
evidence.answer: A draft app must be registered to the SurveyMonkey account to use the API.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Obtain this token in the Settings of your app in the MY APPS tab.
evidence.answer: The access token for a Private app is obtained from the Settings of the app in the MY APPS tab.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The client_secret can be found here.
evidence.answer: The client secret can be found through a link on the page (no location given in text beyond 'here').

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: client_id the unique SurveyMonkey client id you got when registering your app
evidence.answer: The client ID is the unique client ID issued when the app is registered.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: You can set scopes to be required, optional, or not required in your app’s settings .
evidence.answer: Scopes can be set as required, optional, or not required in the app's settings.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: If you have a Private app and will only access your own SurveyMonkey account, you can use the access token, generated when you registered your app, as part of your app’s configuration.
evidence.answer: A Private app accessing only its own account can use the access token generated at registration in its configuration instead of running the OAuth flow.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Private apps are subject to our terms of use .
evidence.answer: Private apps are subject to SurveyMonkey's terms of use.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: If you’re building an app for yourself or your organization, you can deploy a Private app.
evidence.answer: Developers building an app for themselves or their organization can deploy a Private app.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: SurveyMonkey retains the right to reject an app based on criteria not listed above.
evidence.answer: Official docs (not a developer report): SurveyMonkey can reject a public app even on criteria outside its published checklist, and approval does not guarantee compliance.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: Your app should have at least five OAuth sign ins in the first three months.
evidence.answer: Official docs: a public app needs at least five OAuth sign-ins in its first three months to meet the approval checklist, a usage gate before listing.
